title: Waltzes and the Joplin rag book
summary: Laurent and Russell look through his waltzes and a rag book that Charlie Love used to play, and Laurent says he played from memory.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: Ralph, do you have to call up anybody? Yeah, I should think. I'm in the full call. What time is that? About 4.30? We didn't want to take your whole afternoon, but- That's another one of mine. Oh, this is another waltz. Yeah, acceptable waltz.
Acceptable waltz. Oh, yeah. That's one of mine also. Tinklets.
Well, that's the old Redback book. Uh-huh. Yeah. Do you remember, where did you play this Redback book, the Joplin Rags? When did you use that?
Oh, Mean Love used to play that together. Charlie Love, yeah.
He's still trying to get a band together to play that now.
Yeah, Charlie, Charlie. I don't think he'd be able to do it after having that stroke.

That's another one, The Entertainer with Joplin. See, I used to play all them kind of numbers. Oh, yeah. Spring Song by Mendelssohn. Yeah, I used to play all that. I used to play that on my violin when I was a kid.
I used to love that thing. Oh, I used to love that number. And you see, I used to commit all that to memory. I didn't want the music when I was playing out. I committed to memory.
